subject.name: Agricultural Science
subject.description: Agricultural Science syllabus, Form 1-4 (Curriculum Development Centre).

grade.name: Form 1
grade.phase: Secondary — the source scheme itself uses "Form 1" for this level under the 2023 CBC.

topics.name: TOPIC 3: CLIMATE-SMART AGRICUTURE
topics.description: Climate-Smart Agriculture is an approach to agriculture that aims to increase agricultural productivity and improve food security while reducing damage to the environment. This topic introduces learners to climate-smart agriculture, allowing them to evaluate common practices in their local area.

sub_topics.name: Sub-Topic 3 1- Climate-Smart Agriculture
sub_topics.description: Focuses on Climate-Smart Agriculture as an integrated farming approach to increase productivity, improve food security, and minimize greenhouse gas emissions while exploring its key characteristics, benefits, and local factors in Zambia.

competencies.description: Demonstrate understanding of Climate-smart Agriculture.

sub_topics.name: Sub-Topic 3.2- Application of Drones
sub_topics.description: Explores drones as aerial electronic devices equipped with sensors and cameras to collect data on crop health, soil moisture, and weather patterns to improve agricultural productivity sustainably.

competencies.description: Use drones to enhance productivity in agriculture

sub_topics.name: Sub-Topic 3 3 - Climate Change
sub_topics.description: Covers climate change, distinguishing it from climate variability, investigating its natural and human causes, analyzing greenhouse gas effects, and exploring mitigation activities for farmers in Zambia.

competencies.description: Show understanding of climate change and its causes

topics.name: TOPIC 4: FARM STRUCTURES AND MACHINERY
topics.description: Covers buildings, infrastructure, and machinery used to support agricultural activities. Learners view, handle, use, repair, maintain, and properly store garden tools and equipment to ensure longevity and efficiency.

sub_topics.name: Sub-Topic 4 1 - Garden tools and Equipment
sub_topics.description: Examines essential garden tools and equipment, safe handling practices, care, maintenance, storage, identification of knapsack sprayer components, and improvision of garden tools.

competencies.description: Use Garden tools and equipment for better production.

topics.name: TOPIC 5: CROP PRODUCTION
topics.description: Focuses on the fundamentals of crop production and post-harvest management where learners grow selected crops, store, process, add value, and market agricultural produce.

sub_topics.name: Sub-Topic 5.1: Vegetable Production
sub_topics.description: Focuses on growing vegetables for human consumption, covering seed/site selection, vegetable classification, nutritive value, crop rotation design, crop establishment, and post-harvest handling.

competencies.description: Grow a variety of vegetables.

topics.name: TOPIC 5.0 CROP PRODUCTION
topics.description: Crop production is the practice of cultivation of plants for food, fiber, and other products. This topic focuses on the fundamentals of crop production and post-harvest management. Some of the activities in this topic were already covered in term 2. This topic will cover the remaining activities in vegetable production.

competencies.description: Analytical thinking
Communication
Creativity and innovation
Collaboration
Critical Thinking
Environmental sustainability
Problem solving

sub_topics.name: Sub-Topic 5.1: Vegetable Production
sub_topics.description: Vegetable production is the branch of horticulture that focuses on growing vegetables for human consumption. It involves seed/ site selection, seedbed preparation, crop establishment, irrigation, pest and disease management, and harvesting. The goal is to cultivate various edible plant parts, including shoots, leaves, fruits, and roots, for food production.
learning_objectives: 5.1.5 Managing vegetable growing from nursery stage to harvesting (seedbed preparation, sowing/planting, irrigation, weeding, fertilizer application, pest and disease control, harvesting)
5.1.5 Adding value, storing, and marketing vegetables.
5.1.6 Analysing yields and quality of the produce for possible improvement.
5.1.7 Exploring innovative ways of increasing productivity

competencies.description: Grow a variety of vegetables.
Analytical thinking – Learners will be analysing yields for possible improvement
Communicating – Learners will share notes, consult one another, and report findings.
Creativity and innovation – Learners will be making seedbeds and suggesting innovative ways of increasing the productivity of their vegetable production venture.
Collaborating – Learners will be working together to achieve tasks from seedbed preparation to adding value to their produce.

Critical Thinking – Learners will be making critical decisions like determining appropriate depths for sowing seeds and stages of transplanting seedlings, irrigation and other activities to ensure success of the activity.
Environmental sustainability – Learners will be using vegetable production methods that are environmentally friendly.
Problem identifying and managing situations like pests and diseases, seedlings (and hardening), and improvising and repairing tools when needed.

topics.name: TOPIC 6.0: LIVESTOCK PRODUCTION
topics.description: Livestock production is a practice of raising and maintaining domesticated animals primarily for the purpose of producing meat, milk and eggs. By so doing, livestock production contributes significantly to food security, income generation and rural development.

competencies.description: Analytical thinking
Communication
Creativity and innovation
Collaboration
Critical Thinking
Environmental sustainability
Problem solving

sub_topics.name: Sub-Topic 6.1- Importance of Livestock
sub_topics.description: In this subtopic, learners will explore their immediate environment (i.e. local farms) and farming activities that are happening elsewhere through farm visits, participating in agricultural shows, watching videos and studying pictures of farming and farming related activities. By so doing, they will appreciate and demonstrate understanding of the value and challenges of livestock production to the household, community, and nation.
learning_objectives: 6.1.2 Evaluating the economic value of livestock
6.1.3 Exploring the challenges faced in livestock production (Pest and diseases, nutrition, market…)

competencies.description: Demonstrate understanding of the importance of livestock production
Communicating - Learners making presentations on types of livestock and reporting on the economic value of livestock
Collaborating - Learners work together to collect data about livestock and identify challenges.
Critically Thinking - Learners identifying challenges and proposing solutions on livestock production
Problem Solving - Learners finding solutions to the challenges identified
Creativity and Innovation - Learners develop a model solution to livestock production challenges

sub_topics.name: Sub-Topic 6.2 -Nutrition and Feed Formulation in Livestock
sub_topics.description: Farm animals, like all other living things, need feed to maintain life processes. Additionally, they need quality feed to produce the meat, milk, and eggs for which they are reared. The subtopic will introduce learners to the feeds available on the market, the nutritive constituents of feed, the value of feed to livestock, and how feed may be formulated on the farm by visiting farms, feed suppliers, and feed constituent sellers.
learning_objectives: 6.2.1 Identifying different types of livestock feeds
6.2.2 Describing the nutritive value of feed, (proteins, carbohydrate, fats, fiber, minerals, vitamins and water).
6.2.3 Distinguishing between maintenance and production ration

competencies.description: Formulate animal feeds
Analytical thinking – Learners classifying feeds according to intended function (maintenance, production, starter grower, finisher, lactating….)
Communicating - Learners discussing data about available feeds and feed ingredients, and sharing findings on feeds and feed ingredients with others.
Creativity and innovation- Learners will be making rations for named livestock classes.
Collaboration - Learners working with others to inquire about available feeds and feed ingredients and sharing findings on feeds and feed ingredients with others.
Critical Thinking- Learners deciding on what ingredients to mix and the amounts in rations to make.
Problem solving- Learners formulating rations for different categories of animals.
